scope:
Frozen development-only comparison of binary versus absolute CTC product.

Both scores come from the same INT8 invocation. No training, final data,
waveform, audio device or board is accessed.

arm_definitions.control: Binary output of the same dual INT8 model
arm_definitions.phonetic: Binary times absolute CTC P([hey,nyx]); no forced choice

limits: Reused development data and previously observed source populations, not independent acceptance. Pointwise score dominance does not imply fewer latched events, so both continuous event counts are measured. Probability is a model path likelihood, not calibrated human wake probability. The full-history output adds compute; P4 RAM/CPU/latency, real-speaker/room recall and long-call stability are unmeasured. No source WAV reading, speaker playback, microphone capture, board access, PCM-speed change or second audio producer.

audit.limits: Cached-score reconstruction only. Feature-index hashes do not hash the full external scalar feature cache. No new inference, independent wake acceptance, pronunciation, physical endpoint, P4 resource or call stability proof.

negative_audit_test.observed_error: Plan differs from frozen commit or launch

interpretation: Reject the fixed absolute CTC product inference recipe. At.97, matched binary macro proxy recall84.2034% becomes40.2247%, and false near-word views fall from88 to24/3744; continuous events fall from1 to0/7.323822 hours. The best product point in the strict1%/zero-event gate is.99 with only1.53125% macro recall (17/2392 positive variants detected overall). Its highest macro recall anywhere in the original21-point grid is85.2133% at.05, with6 continuous events and9.375% worst-group false views. Retaining ordered output can reject existing errors, but this score loses too much correct speech and fails the unchanged advancement gate. No new score normalization, threshold extension, final scoring or board change follows.
score_binding_note: Both rules use the same dual INT8 artifact and exact invocation history. This export has its own training-only PTQ sample set; the older scalar export is not asserted byte-exact. The matched comparison isolates the frozen inference score on this artifact.
